//: SPEC §12 and the PROMPT's S6 row: the beta ships web-first plus an
Android APK for direct install. `preview` is that APK. The iOS lane is
written and inert: it activates when the Apple Developer enrolment
exists, and the web beta never waits for it.
EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL is the one thing a build has to be told. There is no
model key here and there never will be: the client has no model access
at all, and `cashkit/no-model-access` is an ESLint error that fails CI
if one is ever added (D-MLP-50, S3).
EXPO_PUBLIC_ALLOW_CLOUD_DICTATION is deliberately absent from every
profile. Setting it would put a browser speech vendor on the path, and
SPEC §9 requires that vendor on compliance/subprocessors.md first
The beta lane. `distribution: internal` plus `buildType: apk` is a
file a tester downloads and installs — no Play Store review, no Apple
enrolment, nothing to wait for.
The iOS half of this profile builds only once an Apple team exists;
until then `eas build --platform android --profile preview` is the
whole beta build and it does not need the iOS half to be reachable.
Store distribution. Android is an AAB because Play requires one;
the direct-install APK stays the `preview` profile.
`autoIncrement` with `appVersionSource: remote` means EAS owns the
build number, so two builds from the same commit never collide and
nobody edits a version by hand before a release.
Nothing is configured here yet, and that is correct rather than
incomplete: submission needs an Apple Developer team and a Play
Console service account, and neither exists. The beta does not need
either — an APK is installed from a link.
